body: Timeline, all same session, resident server: 10:25 draft P-01KYER dir=. returns success and grill renders its pack; about 10:32 move refuses lifecycle: unknown item, get answers nf with a different item as nearest, and grep of root .spectackle/work.md and journal.ndjson from the worktree finds ZERO occurrences - server and filesystem agree the record is absent; about 10:35, with no intervening write call from this session, both files contain it and move succeeds. Between the acknowledged write and the visibility window: exec swap 10:31 (self-restart) and adversarial subagents running go test in the same worktree. Smells like the B-01KYD5 lost-update class inverted - a writer holding a stale work.md snapshot wrote LATE, first erasing then restoring the item, or the withWorkLock serialization does not cover one of the writers in play during a swap window. Needs the journal eids around 10:25-10:35 diffed against file mtimes. Verify: reproduce by racing a draft against an exec swap under -self-restart; the acknowledged item must be immediately durable and visible to the next call, every time.

ti: writeWork dedupes refs on untrimmed elements while the reader trims, so duplicates survive one write

note: canonList centralizes the reader per-element canonicalization (trim, drop empty and - placeholder) and writeWork now runs Refs through it BEFORE dedupeStrings, so the refs line written is already a fixed point of the reader. Measured before: Refs [" R-0002","R-0002 ","R-0002","P-0001"] wrote refs:  R-0002, R-0002 , R-0002, P-0001 and reloaded as 4 refs. After: refs: R-0002, P-0001, reloads as 2. splitList delegates to canonList so reader behavior is byte-identical. Needs and Targets deliberately untouched: they carry no duplicate-free contract, and their untrimmed join belongs with the line-grammar work in B-01KYRN4VBEEXQ. No CheckHeader refusal added: canonicalize-on-write closes the writer-reader mismatch without turning a harmless placeholder into a hard Upsert failure. New test asserts the RAW file line, not the reload; the pre-existing test asserted only the reload, which is why the defect survived. Mutation-checked per RECMERGE-003: reverting the writeWork guard fails both subtests.
